meta.title: Hand, Wrist, and Finger Safety in Construction Environments
meta.description: Covers hand hazard recognition, glove selection, tool safety, ergonomics, and employee and employer responsibilities for protecting hands and wrists on construction sites.

hand-safety-intro.title: Introduction to Hand Safety
hand-safety-intro.content: The hand is a complex structure of bones, tendons, nerves, and blood vessels that work together. Even a minor hand injury can affect grip, movement, sensation, and long-term function. Hand injuries are among the most common and preventable workplace injuries on construction sites. Workers must understand hazards, use proper protection, and recognize when hands are at risk.

common-hand-hazards.title: Common Hand Hazards in Construction
common-hand-hazards.content: Construction sites present many hazards that can injure hands, wrists, and fingers. Moving machinery parts can pinch, crush, pull in, or amputate fingers. Sharp tools and materials can cut or puncture. Rough surfaces cause abrasions and blisters. Chemicals can irritate or absorb through skin. Heat, sparks, and flames can cause burns. Vibration can affect circulation and nerve function. The first step in prevention is recognizing these hazards before your hands are exposed.

job-preparation-hand-safety.title: Preparing for the Job
job-preparation-hand-safety.content: Hand safety begins before work starts. Review the task, inspect the area, understand equipment, and confirm proper protection is available. Know what you are working with and where your hands will be placed. Anticipate what can move, shift, rotate, fall, cut, or pinch. Distraction, fatigue, rushing, or overconfidence can lead to injury in a fraction of a second.

tool-equipment-safety.title: Safe Use of Tools and Equipment
tool-equipment-safety.content: Tools can create serious hand hazards if used incorrectly or poorly maintained. Use tools only for their intended purpose. Keep them in good condition. Never bypass guards, remove safety devices, or use damaged equipment. Handles should be comfortable and allow the wrist to remain straight and neutral. Cut away from the body and away from the other hand. Keep guards and shields in place at all times.

gloves-hand-ppe.title: Gloves and Hand Protective Equipment
gloves-hand-ppe.content: No single glove protects against every hazard. Cloth gloves help against minor scratches. Leather gloves protect against rough surfaces and minor burns. Cut-resistant gloves are needed for sharp materials or blades. Heat-resistant gloves are used near flames or hot surfaces. Chemical-resistant gloves are required for corrosive substances, depending on chemical compatibility. Some jobs require additional hand pads, guards, or finger guards. Gloves must not be worn near rotating equipment unless specifically approved, as they can become entangled.

glove-selection-inspection.title: Selecting, Inspecting, and Caring for Gloves
glove-selection-inspection.content: The right glove must fit properly, be inspected before use, and be maintained correctly. Gloves that are too large can become caught in materials or equipment. Gloves that are too small restrict movement and tire the hands. Inspect gloves before each use for holes, tears, contamination, stiffness, cracking, or loss of grip. Replace damaged gloves immediately. OSHA's 2025 rule requires PPE to properly fit construction workers.

ergonomics-responsibilities.title: Ergonomic Hazards and Responsibilities
ergonomics-responsibilities.content: Repetitive motion, forceful gripping, awkward wrist positions, vibration, and prolonged hand-intensive work can cause cumulative injury over time. Symptoms include pain, numbness, tingling, weakness, and reduced grip. Reduce ergonomic stress by alternating tasks, keeping wrists neutral, using properly designed tools, limiting force, and reporting symptoms early. Employers must assess hazards, provide PPE, and train workers. Employees must use required PPE, inspect equipment, follow procedures, and report hazards.

questions.questionText: Which OSHA standard is listed as the primary compliance anchor for hand protection?
A single type of glove can protect workers from all hand hazards.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Which factor should be considered when selecting hand protection?

options.text: The task being performed
The hazards present
The duration of use
All of the above

questions.questionText: A worker is handling sharp-edged sheet metal while wearing thin cloth gloves. What is the concern?

options.text: Cloth gloves offer complete protection for sharp metal edges
Thin cloth gloves may not provide adequate cut resistance; cut-resistant gloves should be used
Thin cloth gloves are adequate as long as the worker moves carefully
Sharp metal is only a hazard when cutting, not when handling finished pieces

questions.questionText: What should you do before using a power tool?

options.text: Check that guards and shields are in place
Confirm the tool is in safe condition
Use the correct PPE
All of the above

questions.questionText: Gloves that are too large can create a hazard because they may reduce control or become caught.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Which glove type is generally most appropriate for corrosive substances, depending on chemical compatibility?

options.text: Chemical-resistant gloves such as rubber, vinyl, neoprene, or other compatible material
Lightweight cloth gloves
Fingerless gloves
Ordinary winter gloves

questions.questionText: A worker notices numbness and tingling in the hands after using a vibrating tool for long periods. What should the worker do?

options.text: Ignore the symptoms and complete the shift before reporting
Apply heat and continue working
Report symptoms to a supervisor and review exposure; use job rotation, reduced exposure, and vibration-reducing PPE as appropriate
Switch to bare-hand work to eliminate the glove variable

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a good ergonomic practice for hand and wrist safety?

options.text: Keep the wrist bent whenever possible to maximize reach
Use forceful gripping for every task regardless of need
Keep the wrist in a neutral position when possible
Ignore hand discomfort unless it becomes severe

questions.questionText: Damaged gloves should be inspected at the end of the shift but may be used until then.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: A worker is asked to clear a jam from a machine that has moving parts that could start unexpectedly. What should happen before reaching into the equipment?

options.text: Reach in quickly between moving cycles to minimize exposure
Ask a coworker to watch for unexpected movement
The machine must be safely shut down and hazardous energy controlled before the worker reaches in
Use thick leather gloves and proceed carefully

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes employee responsibility for hand safety?

options.text: Employees only need gloves if they personally choose to wear them
Employees should use required PPE, follow procedures, inspect gloves, and report hazards
Employees are not responsible for reporting damaged PPE
Employees can remove guards if the job is faster without them

questions.questionText: What is the first step in preventing a hand injury?

options.text: Applying a barrier cream to the hands
Recognizing the hazard before the hands are exposed
Wearing any available glove regardless of the hazard type
Reporting the injury after it occurs

questions.questionText: Gloves should NOT be worn around rotating machinery unless specifically approved for the task because they can become entangled.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Employers are responsible for assessing hand hazards, providing proper PPE, training workers, and enforcing safe procedures.

options.text: True
False

2.questionText: True or False: One universal glove provides adequate protection for every type of hand hazard on a construction site.

options.text: True
False

3.questionText: When choosing hand protection for a construction task, what must be evaluated?

options.text: Only the worker's personal preference
The color of the glove for visibility
The task, the hazards present, and the duration of use
Only whether the gloves are in stock

4.questionText: A worker sustains a cut while handling sharp metal with thin cloth gloves. Which action should have prevented this?

options.text: Working faster to reduce exposure time
Using cut-resistant gloves selected for the sharp-edge hazard
Wearing two pairs of cloth gloves
Applying a barrier cream before handling the metal

5.questionText: Which of the following actions is required before operating a power tool on a construction site?

options.text: Verifying the tool is on the approved vendor list
Confirming the tool is safe, guards are in place, and correct PPE is worn
Checking that the tool has been used before
Cleaning the tool after the previous shift

6.questionText: True or False: Wearing gloves that are too large increases the risk of losing control or getting caught in materials or equipment.

options.text: True
False

7.questionText: A worker is about to handle a corrosive liquid. Which glove material is most appropriate?

options.text: Chemical-resistant material compatible with the specific substance
Thin cotton gloves for dexterity
Fingerless leather gloves
Any glove that fits snugly

8.questionText: After extended use of a vibrating tool, a worker reports hand tingling and numbness. What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Ignore it and finish the shift
Apply ice and continue working
Report symptoms to a supervisor and review vibration controls and job rotation
Remove gloves to see if that resolves the tingling

9.questionText: During a repetitive assembly task, a worker keeps bending the wrist downward. What ergonomic correction is needed?

options.text: Grip harder to compensate for the awkward wrist angle
Rotate the wrist more frequently to loosen the joint
Reposition to keep the wrist straight and neutral
Ignore mild discomfort because it will go away

10.questionText: True or False: A torn or contaminated glove can be worn for the remainder of the shift if no replacement is immediately available.

options.text: True
False

11.questionText: Before clearing a machine jam, what must be confirmed to protect the worker's hands?

options.text: The machine has been idle for at least five minutes
A coworker is present to watch
The machine is safely de-energized and hazardous energy is controlled per lockout/tagout
Thick gloves are on before reaching in

12.questionText: What does employee responsibility for hand safety include?

options.text: Wearing gloves only if personally comfortable
Using required PPE, following procedures, inspecting gloves, and reporting hazards
Deciding when PPE is needed based on personal judgment
Removing machine guards only for assigned tasks

13.questionText: Which approach best prevents hand injuries before they can occur?

options.text: Waiting to see if an injury happens before taking action
Identifying hazards before hands are placed near them
Using any available glove and adjusting later
Reporting near-misses only after the end of the shift

14.questionText: True or False: Any glove can be safely worn near rotating equipment as long as it fits properly.

options.text: True
False

15.questionText: True or False: Under OSHA's PPE standard, employers must assess hazards, select appropriate hand protection, and ensure workers are trained on its use.

options.text: True
